record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equations in the small-dispersion regime ε=ℏ→0 and general smooth initial data, can one solve the non-self-adjoint forward scattering problem and then implement the associated Riemann–Hilbert method to compute the Cauchy problem asymptotically?

evidence.quote: It remains an open problem (see [34]) to solve the forward problem for focusing NLS with general smooth initial data, and then implement the RHP methodology, to obtain the solution of the Cauchy problem in the small dispersion limit ϵ = ℏ ↓ 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation in one space dimension with a small dispersion parameter ε > 0:

    i ε ∂_t ψ + (ε²/2) ∂_x² ψ + |ψ|² ψ = 0,    x ∈ ℝ, t > 0,
    ψ(x, 0; ε) = ψ_0(x),

where ψ_0 ∈ C^∞(ℝ) is a general smooth (e.g., Schwartz-class) initial datum, independent of ε. The associated Zakharov–Shabat spectral problem for focusing NLS is non-self-adjoint, so the eigenvalues of the forward scattering problem may be distributed throughout the complex plane and standard self-adjoint techniques do not apply.

Develop a rigorous method that:

(1) Solves the forward (direct) scattering problem for the non-self-adjoint Zakharov–Shabat operator with potential ψ_0, including a description of the limiting distribution (as ε ↓ 0) of discrete eigenvalues and norming constants together with the continuous-spectrum reflection coefficient, for general smooth ψ_0; and

(2) Uses the resulting scattering data to formulate and asymptotically analyze, via the Riemann–Hilbert/steepest-descent (nonlinear steepest descent or ∂̄) method, the inverse scattering Riemann–Hilbert problem, so as to compute the leading-order asymptotic behavior of ψ(x, t; ε) as ε ↓ 0 for (x, t) in the relevant regions of the (x, t)-plane (including pre- and post-caustic regimes).

In short: solve the non-self-adjoint forward scattering problem for general smooth initial data and implement the Riemann–Hilbert methodology to obtain the small-dispersion (semiclassical) asymptotics of the Cauchy problem for the focusing NLS equation.
artifact.category_tag: semiclassical focusing NLS and Riemann–Hilbert analysis
artifact.status_search_result: The semiclassical limit of focusing NLS via Riemann–Hilbert methods has been carried out rigorously only for special classes of initial data (analytic data via the Kamvissis–McLaughlin–Miller semiclassical soliton ensemble construction; specific families such as square-barrier data; certain analytic real data by Tovbis–Venakides–Bertola and others). For general smooth, non-analytic initial data, the non-self-adjoint forward scattering problem is not understood (eigenvalues are not confined to a curve and WKB-type analyses break down), and a complete RHP-based asymptotic solution of the Cauchy problem remains an outstanding open problem in the field.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical Soliton Ensembles for the Focusing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous RHP-based semiclassical asymptotics carried out for special (analytic) initial data via soliton ensembles.
status_evidence.claim: Existing rigorous results are limited to special analytic initial data, not general smooth data.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical Limit of Focusing NLS for a Family of Square Barrier Initial Data
status_evidence.snippet: Treats a specific family of square-barrier initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Results to date treat restricted families of initial data.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical limit of the focusing NLS: Whitham equations and the Riemann–Hilbert Problem approach
status_evidence.snippet: Whitham/RHP approach applied to particular solutions developing N-phase waves.
status_evidence.claim: RHP approach has been implemented for particular, not general smooth, initial data.
